headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: Mentat can modify shared files while oh-my-openagent injects MCP/hooks and broad egress, creating medium prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads/writes files and shares state via filesystem; oh-my-openagent uses runtime-injected MCPs/hooks and can read project files. That creates a plausible default path where one agent’s file output is consumed by the other as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes severity up from low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or config files
IF oh-my-openagent ingests project files or hooks without provenance filtering
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable hooks/MCP injection for shared runs
Require explicit allowlist for files parsed as instructions
Add provenance tags to agent-generated files
requires-engineering: add content-safety filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys; oh-my-openagent touches session history, provider auth data, and project code, plus sends data to multiple external services. A shared filesystem or workspace can expose code and secrets across the pair, and both agents can transmit context externally. This is a default-path risk, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same project directory or config files
IF either agent forwards file contents or session history to external APIs
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers
Remove secrets from shared directories
Restrict outbound domains for both agents
Rotate provider keys before shared runs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, while oh-my-openagent has broad egress, subprocesses, browser control, and full-permissions mode. The pair can concurrently mutate shared files and repository state via filesystem, with no locking mechanism documented. That makes conflicting writes and irreversible repo corruption plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or config directory
IF git or file writes occur without external locking
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Use per-agent branches
Enable filesystem locks around shared paths
Snapshot the repo before concurrent use
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and oh-my-openagent can act through MCPs and task/message tools. If oh-my-openagent treats Mentat’s proposed edits as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or commits. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so I keep it at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF oh-my-openagent consumes Mentat diffs or summaries without verification
IF downstream tasks or messages are triggered from those outputs
mitigations: Require human review before acting on diffs
Compare proposed edits against tests
Disable auto-commit or auto-send flows
Log source attribution for each instruction
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat is open-source and handles model-provider API keys; oh-my-openagent is open-source but also touches telemetry, installation identifiers, session history, and provider auth data. The main compliance concern is retention and telemetry mismatch on shared code or auth material. No residency or regulated-data evidence is present, so this stays medium.
conditions: IF telemetry or session history includes customer code or secrets
IF retention policies differ for the same project data across the two agents
mitigations: Disable telemetry where possible
Exclude secrets from shared workspaces
Document retention settings for both agents
Purge session history after use
requires-engineering: align data-processing and retention policies
